Rule values written as formulas

Source: R/formula.R
rule-formulas.Rd

Many planning rules state a value as a formula rather than a number: a setback of "0.4 times the wall height, at least 3 m", a floor area ratio of "the front road width times 0.4", a rear yard of "25 per cent of lot depth". Anywhere a rulebook takes a number it also takes a formula, written as a string, e.g. "max(3, 0.4 * H)".

Usage

rule_formula_vars(x)

eval_rule_value(value, vars = list())

Arguments

x

A formula string.

value

A number or a formula string.

vars

A named list of variable values. Vectors are allowed and recycled, so a formula can be evaluated for many sites or storeys at once.

Value

rule_formula_vars() returns the variable names a formula uses. eval_rule_value() returns a numeric vector.

Details

Formulas are restricted: they are parsed, checked against a fixed list of variables and functions, and evaluated without access to anything else, so a rulebook from an untrusted source cannot run arbitrary code.

Variables

H

Height above ground of the storey being tested (m).

storey

Storey number, 1 at ground.

site_area

Site area (m2).

site_depth, site_width

Site depth and width (m).

frontage

Length of road frontage (m).

n_frontages

Number of roads the site fronts.

road_width

Width of the road reserve in front of the site (m).

slope

Average site slope (per cent).

distance

Distance to the feature named in the rule (m).

corner

1 on a corner site, otherwise 0.

Functions

Arithmetic (+ - * / ^), comparison (< <= > >= == !=), &, |, !, and min(), max(), abs(), floor(), ceiling(), round(), sqrt(), ifelse(), clamp(x, lo, hi), step(x, breaks, values) (the value of the band x falls in) and interp(x, xs, ys) (straight-line interpolation between points).

Examples

eval_rule_value("max(3, 0.4 * H)", list(H = c(5, 10, 20)))
#> [1] 3 4 8
eval_rule_value("road_width * 0.4", list(road_width = 8))
#> [1] 3.2
eval_rule_value(12)
#> [1] 12
rule_formula_vars("max(3, 0.4 * H) + 0 * site_area")
#> [1] "H"         "site_area"
